analysis: Examined the two base_text units of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json (base lines 2005-3777). The visible patch changes are limited to prompt_contract_id and chain_hash values, with similar edits at many other lines. The visible excerpt is a synthetic public test-vector update: the prompt_contract_id changes from 6bb9fb05... to 8171fec3..., and block-boundary chain hashes change accordingly. No secrets, credentials, attestation material, keys or executable code appear in the supplied text. The content is public synthetic cache-parity input, tool schemas and token ids. This fixture does not touch the provider/coordinator trust boundary directly (TB-002, TB-011, A-016). It could matter indirectly to the prefix-cache threat T-041, because the prompt contract id and chain hashes feed cache keying and boundaries. Only the fixture was supplied, so the producer and consumer code that uses these vectors was not visible. The patch excerpt and range map are truncated (range_map_complete=false), so changes outside the visible excerpt were not fully seen. Open questions for integration: (1) whether the Go coordinator and Swift provider implementations of the prompt-contract hash were updated in lockstep, so cache-key domain separation and the contract-id derivation are consistent; (2) whether the contract id still binds all template-affecting inputs, so cross-tenant cache sharing cannot collide. These are unverified contracts rather than observed regressions, and no finding is raised.
